Daily Run Rate: Average Studio credits per calendar day across the observed history window. Missing dates inside that span count as zero usage rather than inflating an active-day average.
Projected Credits (30d): First forecast month, using the same fitted or selected growth rate as the projection chart.
Projected Cost (30d): Projected 30-day cost, valued at the blended rate implied by the actual prepaid / pay-as-you-go split rather than a single assumed price.
Projected Cost by Agent (12mo): This agent's slice of the projected twelve-month cost, allocated by its share of consumption. Same assumption as the 30-day version: the mix between agents is taken to hold.
Projected Cost by Agent (30d): This agent's slice of the projected 30-day cost. The per-agent export carries no date, so an agent cannot have its own run rate. This allocates the tenant projection by the agent's share of consumption instead, which assumes the mix between agents holds. Fine for sizing, wrong for an agent that is ramping or being retired.
Projected Cost by Group (12mo): This group's slice of the projected twelve-month cost, allocated by its share of user-attributed consumption.
Projected Cost by Group (30d): This group's slice of the projected 30-day cost. The per-user export carries no date, so this allocates the tenant projection by the group's share of user-attributed consumption. Only covers credits that reached a named user - agent and environment activity with no person attached is not in the share, so these will not sum to the tenant total.
Projected Credits (Horizon): Sum of forecast months over the selected planning horizon, using the same fitted or selected growth rate as the projection chart.
Studio Days Observed: Distinct days on which any Studio consumption was recorded. The export only contains days with activity, so this is the true observation count.
Studio Entitlement Days Remaining: How long the prepaid capacity lasts at the current daily rate. Counts only environments that hold capacity - an environment with none cannot run one down. Blank when there is no prepaid capacity to burn through.
Studio Forecast Confidence: History-length and coverage indication. A fit needs at least 28 calendar days and 7 days with positive consumption; sparse or shorter windows remain low confidence. This is not a statistical prediction interval.
Studio Forecast Note: States whether the projection uses historical fitting, a selected scenario, or a flat fallback because usable history is insufficient. Also discloses the missing-day assumption and growth bounds.
Studio Forecast Summary: Written summary of the Studio outlook, filter-aware. Leads with the twelve month number so it answers the page title.
Studio Growth Applied %: On **Fitted from history**, uses the fitted monthly rate when history is sufficient; otherwise falls back to flat and explains why. Manual scenarios keep their selected rates.
Studio Fitted Monthly Growth %: Fits a log trend to the seven-day rolling average of dated tenant consumption. Requires at least 28 calendar days and 7 positive-consumption days. Missing dates inside the span are treated as zero; fitted monthly growth is bounded to -30%/+30% for planning.
Studio History Span Days: Calendar span between the first and last dated observations in scope, and the fraction of that span with recorded rows. Environment and selected-period filters remain in scope.
Studio Month Cost: Cost of that month at the blended rate actually being achieved across the measured prepaid and pay-as-you-go split.
Studio Month Credits: Credits expected in a given month ahead, growing a 30-day run rate forward at the applied rate.
Studio Sessions Proxy: Distinct days with recorded Studio activity in the current selection.
Studio Year Cost: Cost over the next twelve months at today's achieved blended rate.
Studio Year Credits: Credits projected over the next twelve months, compounding the chosen growth rate month on month.
Agents without User Activity: Agents present in the per-agent export but with no recorded user activity - typically system or orchestration agents.
Avg Agents per User: Agents touched per user - a breadth-of-adoption signal within Studio.
Org Filter Status: Plain statement of whether the Group By control will reach the Studio figures on this page, and which grains it cannot reach.
Org Match Rate: Share of Studio users that resolve to a record in the org dimension. Studio reports a work email and the org export a UPN; in most tenants these are the same string, but they need not be. A low figure here means slicing Studio by department will silently drop people.
Studio Users with Copilot Licence: Studio users who also hold a Microsoft Copilot licence.
Agent Credit Share %: This agent's share of all consumed Studio credits in the current view.
Billed Credit Ratio: The share of an agent's credits that were chargeable. High is not necessarily bad - it means the agent's work falls outside what prepaid capacity covers. Shown as "Charged %".
Billing Active Users: Distinct people who consumed at least one Studio credit.
Billing Agents with Credits: Distinct agents appearing in the billing actuals.
Billing Period: Coverage window of the loaded export, inferred from Usage_Date. The per-agent and per-user exports carry no date, so this states the period every figure on the page refers to.
Group Credit Share %: This group's share of user-attributed Studio credits. Separate from User Credit Share % because the denominator has to clear the Group By and Org tables too. A visual grouped by Group By[Group] filters through Org, so clearing only the fact table leaves the denominator scoped to the group and every share reads 100%.
Studio Consumed Credits (Tenant): All Studio credits consumed: prepaid plus pay-as-you-go.
Studio Entitled Capacity: Credits bought up front for an environment. Microsoft calls this "entitlement" in the Studio admin centre; the report says "Prepaid capacity" to match the word used on the Cowork pages for the same idea. Real money, unlike the user and policy limits on Cowork, which are only caps. The export repeats this on every daily row, so this reads the latest value per environment rather than summing across days.
Studio Entitlement Headroom: Prepaid credits still unused, across environments that hold any. Shown as "Prepaid left". Environments with no prepaid capacity bill directly and are excluded rather than dragging this negative.
Studio Entitlement Utilisation %: How much of the prepaid capacity has been used, across environments that hold any. Over 100% means prepaid is exhausted and usage has spilled onto pay-as-you-go. Shown as "Prepaid used %".
Studio PAYG Consumed: Pay-as-you-go credits consumed above entitlement, billed as overage. Gated on the selected period, but narrowing rather than replacing existing date context so the figure still varies along a date axis.
Studio Prepaid Consumed: Prepaid credits consumed, drawn from committed entitlement capacity. Gated on the selected period, but narrowing rather than replacing existing date context so the figure still varies along a date axis.
Studio Prepaid Cost: Cost of Studio consumption drawn from prepaid capacity packs.
Studio Prepaid Share %: Share of Studio spend covered by prepaid capacity rather than billed as pay-as-you-go overage.
Studio Total Credits Used: All credits used across users, billable or not.
Total Billable Cost: Headline Studio cost: prepaid and pay-as-you-go consumption each valued at their own rate. The entitlement export gives the split as measured fact, so this does not assume a single blended price.
Total Billable Credits Used: The chargeable portion of user consumption.
Total Billed Credits: Credits the customer is actually charged for.
Total Non-Billed Credits: Credits consumed inside entitlement and therefore not charged.
User Credit Share %: This user's share of all Studio credits in the current view.
Agent Action: Recommended action for an agent, combining how much it consumes with how much of that consumption is actually chargeable. These labels must stay character-identical to 'Agent Action Group'[Action], which the Agents by Recommended Action chart matches against.
Agents in Action: Number of agents whose current recommended action matches this label. Mirrors User Count on the Cowork seat chart. Counts agents from the per-agent export rather than the agent bridge. The bridge also carries agents seen only in the per-user export, and those have no agent-grain consumption to classify - they would land in "Unused" purely because they are missing from this file.
Agents with No Consumption: Agents present in the export that consumed nothing at all - typically built and then abandoned.
Consumption Without Entitlement: Credits used in environments that hold no prepaid capacity at all, so every credit bills directly. Shown as "Credits with no prepaid cover".
Cost in Action: Billable cost of the agents sitting in this recommended action, so the chart can show what each group is worth in money as well as headcount.
Cost per Consumed Credit: Average cost of every credit an agent consumes, billed or not. Reveals which agents are genuinely expensive rather than merely busy.
Cost per Studio User: Studio cost attributable to each consuming person.
Credits in Action: Credits consumed by the agents sitting in this recommended action, for use as a tooltip on the Agents by Recommended Action chart.
Entitlement Absorbed %: The share of an agent's credits covered by prepaid capacity, so they never reached a bill. Shown as "Covered, not charged".
Environments In Use: Environments carrying real consumption, so tables can drop the empty ones.
Environments Without Entitlement: How many environments are consuming credits without any prepaid capacity behind them.
Features Used: Distinct billable features an agent draws on. Breadth here usually means a richer agent, and a more expensive one.
Studio Concentration Summary: Plain-language reading of how concentrated Studio usage is.
Studio Headline: The single most important thing about Studio spend right now, stated in words. Names the environment carrying most consumption and whether it sits inside an entitlement, because that is what decides the bill.
Studio PAYG Share %: Share of consumption billed as pay-as-you-go overage rather than drawn from prepaid entitlement. A rising value means capacity is undersized.
Studio Top 10% Share: Share of Studio credits used by the heaviest 10% of users. Studio adoption is usually far more concentrated than Cowork.
Unlicensed Credits: Studio credits consumed by people who hold no M365 Copilot licence. Worth knowing: it is demand that a licence purchase would not remove.
GHCP Billing Period: Coverage window of the figures on the page, so a reader never has to guess what 'credits' refers to. Mirrors the Billing period tag on the Studio pages.
GHCP Period Label: Names the window in prose, for subtitles and narrative cards.
GHCP Period Months: Whole calendar months of history in scope. Zero means everything exported. Defaults to zero so every existing figure is unchanged until someone narrows the window.
GHCP Period Start: First date still in scope, for measures to filter against. Snaps to the 1st of a month rather than counting days back, because the credit pool resets on the 1st - a window that starts mid-month would be compared against a full month's allowance.
GHCP Forecast Confidence: Confidence in the GitHub Copilot projection, based on how many months of history the fitted growth rate has to work with.
GHCP Latest Month Credits: Credits consumed in the most recent complete month inside the selected period. The basis for every forward-looking figure on the forecast page.
GHCP Observed Growth %: Observed month-on-month growth in credit consumption, fitted across the selected period. Blank when only one month is in scope - a single point cannot describe a trend.
GHCP Overage From September: What the latest month's consumption would cost once the promotional allowance ends on 1 September 2026 - same usage, smaller pool. This is the single most useful number on the page: a tenant reviewing a zero-overage bill today has no other way to see it coming.
GHCP Year Credit Share %: How much of the twelve-month projection is credits drawn beyond the included allowance, as opposed to fixed seat cost.
GHCP Monthly Pool: Credits included with the seats held, pooled enterprise-wide. This is a pool, not a per-person entitlement. One developer's unused allowance covers another's excess, so there is no such thing as a developer being individually over their limit.
GHCP Pool Change %: How far the pool changes at the allowance change date. Zero when the tenant is already on the standard entitlement.
GHCP Pool From September: The pool that applies from the allowance change date, using the standard per-plan entitlements. Both the date and the entitlements are parameters - see Settings.
GHCP Pool Headroom: Credits left in this month's pool at the latest month's consumption. Negative would mean the pool is already exhausted.
GHCP Pool Used %: How much of the shared pool the latest month consumed.
GHCP Active Developers: Developers who consumed at least one AI credit in the selected period.
GHCP Credits Used: AI credits consumed through GitHub Copilot in the selected period. Code completions and next-edit suggestions are unlimited on every paid plan and never appear here, so completion volume is not a cost driver.
GHCP Days Observed: Distinct days on which any GitHub Copilot consumption was recorded, within the selected period.
GHCP Licensed Developers: Developers holding a Copilot seat, whether or not they used it.
GHCP Months Observed: Distinct calendar months present in the selected period. Counting days and dividing by 28 overstates the monthly rate, because the export only carries working days - about 20 a month, not 28.
GHCP Allowance Absorbed: The portion of consumption absorbed by the included allowance and therefore never billed. GitHub computes this server-side, so unlike the Cowork prepaid split it is measured rather than assumed.
GHCP Gross Value: What the consumption would be worth with no allowance behind it. NOT a cost. Most or all of it is absorbed by the credits included with the seats, so it is shown as "Usage value (not billed)" rather than sitting in a cost row where it would read as a bill.
GHCP Overage Cost: Credit consumption beyond the shared pool, billed pay-as-you-go at the rate in Settings. GitHub calls this overage; it is the same mechanism as Cowork pay-as-you-go, so the report uses one term for both.
GHCP Overage Share %: Share of consumption that fell outside the included allowance.
GHCP Seat Cost (Monthly): Seat cost per month. Copilot Business is $19 a seat, Enterprise $39. For most tenants this dwarfs credit overage, so a cost page that shows only credits misses where the money actually goes.
GHCP Total Cost: Total cost of running GitHub Copilot: seats plus any credit overage.
GHCP Basis Note: Plain statement of what the GHCP figures rest on and what they exclude.
GHCP Concentration Summary: Where credit consumption is concentrated, in words.
GHCP Cost Headline: One line stating where GitHub Copilot cost actually sits, so the page opens with a sentence rather than a number.
GHCP Forecast Summary: Plain-English summary of the GitHub Copilot forecast. Every figure is read from the model, including how much history the fitted rate is based on.
GHCP September Cliff: What happens to the included AI credit allowance when the published rates change. Reads the date and the standard allowances from 'GHCP Allowance Change', says nothing is pending if this tenant is already on standard rates, and switches to past tense once the date has passed. VAR names avoid Today and Lead: both are DAX functions, and a colliding VAR name breaks every query on the model rather than just this measure.
GHCP Coding Agent Share %: Share of credits consumed by autonomous coding agent runs rather than interactive chat. Agent work is billed under its own SKU and behaves very differently - it runs unattended, so it scales with jobs, not with people.
GHCP Cost per Developer: Monthly cost of a seat plus its share of any overage.
GHCP Powerful Model Share %: Share of credits spent on the most expensive model tier. High-end models cost roughly ten times a lightweight one per token, so a large share here is the biggest single lever on credit consumption.
GHCP Seat Cost With No Credit Use: Monthly seat cost carried by developers who consumed no credits in the selected period.
GHCP Seats With No Credit Use: Seats held by developers who consumed no credits at all in the period. Completions are unlimited and unmetered, so a developer can be genuinely productive and still appear here - treat it as a prompt to check, not proof the seat is wasted.
GHCP Top 10% Share: Share of credits consumed by the heaviest 10% of developers. A high figure means pool pressure is driven by a small group, so enablement or guardrails aimed at them move the number more than anything org-wide.
All Cost /mo: All three products' monthly cost added together. Cowork and Studio are credit consumption; GitHub is mostly seats, which is why it dominates.
All Credits /mo: All three products' monthly credit run rate added together.
All Products Headline: One line on what the combined page can and cannot tell you.
Combined Caveat: Why the combined figures understate Copilot Studio. Adapts to whether any unattributed Studio credits are actually present in this tenant's export.
Cowork Cost /mo: Cowork cost normalised to a month.
Cowork Credits /mo: Cowork credits normalised to a month. The three products are exported over different windows - Cowork 13 weeks, GitHub 3 months, Studio 9 days - so raw totals cannot be compared. Every figure on the combined page is a monthly run rate for that reason.
GHCP Cost /mo: GitHub Copilot cost normalised to a month: seats plus any credit overage. Seats are already a monthly figure; overage is averaged over the months in the selection.
GHCP Credits /mo: GitHub Copilot credits normalised to a month, from the calendar months actually present in the selection.
Source Windows: States the window each product was exported over, so nobody reads the combined figures as like-for-like actuals.
Studio Cost /mo: Copilot Studio cost normalised to a month, for credits attributed to a named user.
Studio Credits /mo: Copilot Studio credits normalised to a month, from the days observed. Covers only credits attributed to a named user - the agent and environment exports carry no person, so this is a floor rather than the whole picture.
Cowork Capacity Pack Balance Value: Prepaid Capacity Pack credits available to draw down. The Cost page slicer overrides the deployment setting, so a reader can model buying a pack without changing the tenant's configuration.
Cowork PAYG Rate Value: Cowork pay-as-you-go rate in force. Keeps its original name so every measure that already prices against it is unaffected by the move.
Cowork Prepaid Discount %: How much cheaper a prepaid credit is than a pay-as-you-go one.
Cowork Prepaid Rate Value: Cowork prepaid rate in force. Only bites when a pack balance is set.
GitHub Allowance Change Date: The date the included GitHub AI credit allowance changes.
GitHub Business Seat Value: Monthly list price of a Copilot Business seat.
GitHub Business Standard Value: Included credits per Copilot Business seat from the change date.
GitHub Enterprise Seat Value: Monthly list price of a Copilot Enterprise seat.
GitHub Enterprise Standard Value: Included credits per Copilot Enterprise seat from the change date.
GitHub Rate Value: GitHub Copilot pay-as-you-go rate per AI credit, once the included allowance is exhausted.
Rates In Use: One line a reader can check the figures against, since the rates are no longer visible as slicers.
Studio Effective Rate: Blended Studio rate actually achieved across the measured prepaid and pay-as-you-go split.
Studio PAYG Rate Value: Copilot Studio pay-as-you-go rate in force.
Studio Prepaid Discount %: Discount the prepaid Studio rate earns against pay-as-you-go.
Studio Prepaid Rate Value: Copilot Studio prepaid rate in force. This one matters even with no pack balance entered, because the Studio export reports the prepaid and pay-as-you-go split as measured fact rather than as an assumption.
Cowork Period Label: Names the window in prose, for chart subtitles and narrative cards.
Cowork Period Weeks: Weeks of history in scope. Defaults to the four-week billing period, so every existing figure is unchanged until someone widens the window.
Studio Period Days: Days of history in scope. Zero means everything that was exported.
Studio Period Start: The earliest usage date still in scope, for measures to filter against.
Cowork Forecast Summary: Plain-English summary of the Cowork forecast. Every figure, including the length of the fitting window, is read from the model - nothing about this tenant is written into the text.
Growth Applied %: The monthly growth rate the projection uses. Defaults to the rate fitted from 13 weeks of actual usage; move the slider to test a different rate.
Growth Is Override: True when the reader has overridden the fitted rate, so the page can say so.
Month Cost $: Cost of that month at the rate actually being achieved today, so a Capacity Pack discount carries through into the projection.
Month Credits: Credits expected in a given month ahead, growing the current period forward at the applied rate.
Year Cost $: Cost over the next twelve months at today's achieved rate.
Year Credits: Credits expected over the next twelve months.
Forecast Accuracy (Backtest): Honest self-assessment: fit on all but the last four weeks, then score the prediction against those held-out weeks.
Implied Monthly Growth %: Weekly growth implied by the fit, restated monthly so it can be compared directly with the growth scenario picker.
Residual SD: Standard deviation of the fit residuals — drives the confidence band.
Trend Intercept: Regression baseline used to calculate fitted values. Internal maths with no business meaning on its own.
Trend R2: Goodness of fit. Below about 0.6 the linear projection should be treated as indicative only.
Trend Slope: Least-squares gradient of weekly credits against week index — the growth rate the data actually supports, as opposed to the slider guess.
Cowork Prepaid Rate: Now delegates to the Prepaid Rate what-if parameter. Previously this was the hard-coded literal 0.008; the parameter defaults to that same value, so existing figures are unchanged until someone moves the slider.
Cost Title: Chart title that names the chosen grouping, replacing the dynamic header a field parameter would have given.
GHCP Growth Applied %: The month-on-month growth rate used by the forecast. Follows the Growth Assumption slicer; with no selection, or on "Fitted from history", it uses the rate actually observed in this tenant's own usage.
GHCP Latest Usage Date: The last day on which any GitHub Copilot credit was drawn, within the selected period. Anchors the projection - month 1 is the month after this.
GHCP Month Cost: Projected total spend in projection month N - seats plus any credits drawn beyond that month's allowance.
GHCP Month Credit Cost: Projected pay-as-you-go credit spend in projection month N: whatever the month's credits exceed that month's allowance, at the published rate.
GHCP Month Credits: Projected credits for month N of the next twelve, growing the most recent full month at the chosen rate.
GHCP Month Pool: The included credit allowance that applies in projection month N. Steps down automatically for months at or beyond the allowance change date held in Settings.
GHCP Year Cost: Total projected spend across the next twelve months - twelve months of seats, plus credits beyond the allowance applying in each month.
GHCP Year Credits: Total projected credits across the next twelve months.
Grouped By: Name of the attribute currently chosen, for chart titles. Reads "several attributes" if more than one is selected, which would double-count people.
Trend Window Weeks: How many weeks the Cowork trend line is actually fitted over. Mirrors the filter context used by [Trend Slope] and [Implied Monthly Growth %] so any prose quoting the window stays true to whatever history is loaded.
Lapsed Users (Week): Users active last week who did not return this week.
Multi-Service %: Share of active users who touch more than one service - a depth-of-adoption signal.
Multi-Service Users: Users touching more than one service. Multi-service users are typically far stickier than single-service ones.
New Users (Week): Users appearing for the very first time in the week in context.
WoW Retention %: Share of last week's active users who were also active this week.
Credits Over Policy Allowance: Credits that would be refused because a policy reached its monthly spending limit. Users on that policy lose access to agents until credits reset on the 1st. Measured over the current billing period, because the configured limit is monthly.
Person Allowance: Adds up each person's own monthly credit limit. This is a governance cap, not capacity anyone paid for - going over it is a policy event, not a bill. Shown as "User limits". Do not confuse with Policy Allowance, which adds up the limits on spending policies instead and gives a different number.
Person Allowance Used %: Credits used as a share of the sum of people's own monthly limits. Over 100% means people collectively used more than their personal caps allowed. Shown as "Used vs user limits".
Person Headroom: Credits still available before people hit their own monthly limits. Governance headroom, not money already spent.
Policies Over Allowance: Spending policies whose current-period consumption has passed their configured monthly limit. Users on these policies lose agent access until the 1st of next month.
Policy Allowance: Adds up the plan limits on the spending policies. A separate governance layer from Person Allowance - policies cap a group, user limits cap a person, and the two totals differ. Shown as "Policy limits".
Policy Allowance Used %: Credits used as a share of the spending policy limits. Over 100% means consumption exceeded what the policies allow. Shown as "Used vs policy limits" - a different denominator from Person Allowance Used %.
Policy Headroom: Credits still available before consumption exceeds the spending policy limits. Shown as "Credits left".
Billing Basis: How this period is actually billed. Derived from the prepaid balance against consumption, so it never has to be declared.
Blended Rate $: The price actually paid per credit across both rates. Equals the pay-as-you-go rate when no prep aid balance is held.
Cowork PAYG Cost: What the pay-as-you-go portion cost, after any prepaid balance was used up.
Cowork PAYG Credits: Consumption billed at the pay-as-you-go rate, once prepaid is exhausted.
Cowork PAYG Share of Cost %: Share of spend still going through pay-as-you-go. A high share means a Capacity Pack would likely reduce the bill.
Cowork Prepaid Balance: Prepaid Capacity Pack credits available to draw down. Sourced from the Capacity Pack Balance input, because no Viva export carries the balance - it lives in admin centre under Cost management > Billing method. Automatically zero under pay-as-you-go only, where no packs are in play. Prepaid Capacity Pack credits available to draw down. Enter the balance shown in admin centre un der Cost management. Zero means everything bills pay-as-you-go.
Cowork Prepaid Cost: What the prepaid draw-down cost. Zero when no Capacity Pack balance is held.
Cowork Prepaid Left: Prepaid credits still unused. Money already spent that is not yet working.
Cowork Prepaid Used: Consumption drawn from the prepaid balance. Prepaid is always consumed before pay-as-you-go.
Cowork Total Cost: Consumption that falls inside the prepaid commitment. What the period actually costs: prepaid credits at the prepaid rate, the rest at the pay-as-you- go rate.
Seat Saving Basis Note: States the basis used to price the right-sizing opportunity, so the number on the page is never read as a cash refund.
Allocated Cost: What to charge back: the prepaid share at the prepaid rate plus the rest at the pay-as-you-go rate. Its total over every cost centre is Cowork Total Cost. Use it rather than Cowork Total Cost by cost centre, which would give every cost centre the whole capacity pack.
Allocated Cost Share %: This row's share of the Allocated Cost of everything selected.
Allocated Credits: Credits used in the period by the people in scope, each charged to their own spending policy for the whole period.
Allocated PAYG Cost: Allocated PAYG Credits at the pay-as-you-go rate.
Allocated PAYG Credits: The pay-as-you-go part of Allocated Credits: what the capacity pack did not cover.
Allocated Prepaid Cost: Allocated Prepaid Credits at the prepaid rate.
Allocated Prepaid Credits: The prepaid part of Allocated Credits: its share of the capacity pack, pro rata.
Chargeback $: List-price cost: credits used at the pay-as-you-go rate, ignoring any capacity pack. For what to charge each cost centre, use Allocated Cost.
Chargeback Prepaid Share %: The tenant's prepaid share for the period: prepaid credits used divided by all credits used, across every person whatever the policy, org or Group By filters. Each cost centre is charged this share of its credits at the prepaid rate.
Chargeback: Overage only: the cost of credits used above each person's allowance (Over Limit $). For what to charge each cost centre, use Allocated Cost.
Chargeback %: Overage as a share of allowance: credits used above each person's allowance divided by the allowance.
Avg Weekly Active Users: Average number of people active each week across the selected Cowork period. Uses the same window and seat scoping as Consuming Users, so it can never exceed it. Weekly Active Users counts anyone active in any loaded week when no week is in context, which is why it is not used on a card.
Consuming Users: People who consumed the selected service in the selected period. Differs from User Count, which counts everyone holding a seat whether they used it or not.
Cowork Total Credits Used: Credits consumed in the selected period, defaulting to the current billing period.
Action Meaning: What acting on this recommendation actually means, in one short phrase. Sits beside the number so a reader never has to infer the action from the bucket name.
Action Value /mo: Monthly value of acting on the recommendation, and nothing else. Right-Size Net $ is generic headroom arithmetic: it subtracts one column from another for whoever is in scope, so slicing it by action returned that group's unused headroom rather than the value of doing what the row says. That is why 'Correctly sized' showed a $5,739 saving and 'Hold' showed $620. Here only the actionable buckets carry a number: 1 reclaim -> the whole seat is released 2 review -> the whole seat, if the check confirms it 3 downsize -> the oversized portion is released 6 upgrade -> negative, because funding those people costs money 4 hold / 5 monitor / 7 correctly sized -> nothing, by definition
Actioned Seats: Seats with a recommendation that carries a monthly value: reclaim, review, downsize or upgrade (actions 1, 2, 3 and 6). The seat count behind Right-Size Net $.
Additional Credits Needed: Capacity required to properly fund users who persistently exceed their current seat.
Dormant Seat $: Value of dormant capacity. Only a real saving under prepaid or hybrid - see Seat Saving Basis Note.
Dormant Seat Credits: Assigned capacity tied up in seats that were never used this period.
Dormant Seats: Seats with no consumption at all in the four-week billing snapshot. Not proof the seat is unused - it is one period, and the Period control does not reach this figure. Treat it as a list to check, not a list to cancel.
Licensed but Inactive: Licensed people with no consumption in the four-week billing snapshot - a licence-management question rather than a capacity one. Not "never used": someone idle this period may have used Cowork earlier. Seat Action's "1. Reclaim - never used" is the never-used count.
Oversized Seats $: Monthly value released by downsizing oversized seats ("3. Downsize"): only the portion above the recommended limit. The same branch as Action Value /mo.
Reclaimable $: Value of reclaimable capacity. Only a real saving under prepaid or hybrid - see Seat Saving Basis Note.
Reclaimable Credits: Credits released if every oversized seat were resized to its 90th-percentile week. Excludes seats that need upgrading.
Right-Size Net $: Value released each month by acting on every recommendation: reclaims and downsizes, less the cost of the upgrades. Positive is a net saving. Equals Unused Seats $ + Oversized Seats $ + Upgrade Seats $. Prefer it to Reclaimable $, which resizes every seat and is not scoped to the recommendation.
Seats to Downsize: Active users whose seat materially exceeds what they consume.
Seats to Upgrade: People persistently exceeding their seat, who are genuinely under-provisioned rather than merely spiky.
Unused Seats: Seats recommended to reclaim or review (actions 1 and 2).
Unused Seats $: Monthly value of the seats nobody is using: "1. Reclaim - never used" and "2. Review - no usage in billing period", each at its full limit. The same branches as Action Value /mo, so it ties to the Financial impact table.
Upgrade Seats $: Monthly cost of upgrading people who are persistently over their seat ("6. Upgrade - persistently over"). Negative, because it is spend rather than a saving. The same branch as Action Value /mo.
Cowork Concentration Summary: Plain-language reading of how concentrated consumption is, phrased the way a business reader would say it out loud.
Cowork Forecast Confidence: Hashed Viva person identifier. Use for distinct-person counts where UPN is unavailable. Forecast reliability expressed as a word rather than a coefficient. Combines how closely history follows a steady pattern with how accurate the model proved when tested against weeks it had never seen.
Cowork Forecast Confidence Note: What the confidence rating means for planning, in plain words.
Growth Summary: Weekly growth restated as a sentence fragment usable in a card subtitle.
Steadiness: Steadiness expressed in words, for readers who should not have to know what a coefficient of variation is.
Anomaly Flag: Marks weeks that fall far outside the normal pattern and are worth investigating. Shown on the page as 'Unusual week'.
Consumption Gini: Gini coefficient of credit consumption. 0 = perfectly even, 1 = one person consumes everything.
Cowork Top 10% Share: Share of credits consumed by the heaviest 10% of users. High values mean the run-rate depends on a handful of people.
Credits per Session: Average credits consumed per session - a session-intensity signal.
Top 1% Share: Share of credits consumed by the heaviest 1% of users - a key-person dependency signal.
Ungoverned $: Spend recorded against no spending policy - usage that fell outside any policy window. A governance gap to close.
Ungoverned %: Share of credits falling outside policy control.
Ungoverned Credits: Credits recorded against the all-zero policy GUID — usage that fell outside any spending policy window. A governance gap.
Volatility (CV): Weekly coefficient of variation. High = unpredictable spend needing a budget buffer. Low = safe to commit capacity against.
Z-Score (Week): How far the week in context sits from that group's own mean, in standard deviations. Feeds the anomaly tripwire.
Cowork Weekly Cost: What each week actually cost. Cowork Total Cost deliberately strips week context so it can honour the Period slicer, which makes it flat on a date axis. This reads the weekly grain instead, so it can be trended. Prepaid capacity is drawn down oldest week first, so a week only bills at the pay-as-you-go rate once the pack is exhausted. With no pack balance entered it reduces to credits x the pay-as-you-go rate.
Cowork Weekly PAYG Cost: The pay-as-you-go portion of a week's cost - what the prepaid pack did not cover. Stacks with Cowork Weekly Prepaid Cost to give Cowork Weekly Cost. With no pack balance entered this is the whole weekly cost, which is the correct answer for a pay-as-you-go tenant.
Cowork Weekly Prepaid Cost: The prepaid portion of a week's cost. Cowork Prepaid Cost is a period total - it strips week context so it can honour the Period slicer - so it renders flat on a weekly axis and cannot be stacked. This reads the weekly grain instead. The pack is drawn down oldest week first, so early weeks are prepaid and later weeks fall through to pay-as-you-go once it is exhausted.
Credits 4wk Rolling Avg: Average weekly credits over this week and the three before it - a smoothing line that removes single-week noise. Early weeks divide by however many weeks actually exist, so the line is not artificially deflated at the start of the series.
Weekly Active Users: Distinct people who consumed credits during the week.
Weekly Credits: Total credits consumed in the week under the current filters.
